result.title: CoRA-Bench: Evaluating Evidence Preservation by Context Selectors Under Token Budgets
result.comment: Paper Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: Long-Context Foundation Models
result.summary: Context selection can reduce input length during long-input inference but can remove evidence required to answer a query. We introduce CoRA-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating evidence preservation under shared token budgets. We compare head and tail truncation, BM25, dense retrieval, dense retrieval with reranking, LLMLingua-2, and Provence across BABILong, LOONG Financial Spotlight, a custom NoLiMa diagnostic, and LongMemEval. Evidence-preservation results reveal task-dependent tradeoffs: BM25 achieves 0.921 supporting-fact recall on BABILong at 128K, dense retrieval and dense reranking each achieve 0.908 needle recall on NoLiMa at 64K, and dense retrieval achieves 0.993 answer-bearing-turn recall on LongMemEval at 64K. Evidence, token retention, and complementary reader evaluations use the same selected contexts. Reader evaluations use dataset-native answer metrics and three runs on the same questions, with paired bootstrap confidence intervals. At a 32K budget, BM25 achieves 46.20% BABILong answer accuracy and dense retrieval achieves 71.13% LongMemEval accuracy. The results show that method rankings vary across evidence types and between evidence recall and downstream accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CoRA-Bench 基准，在相同 token 预算下比较头尾截断、BM25、稠密检索、重排、LLMLingua-2、Provence 等上下文选择器，跨 BABILong、LOONG、NoLiMa 诊断集与 LongMemEval 同时测量证据召回与下游答题准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「共享预算下的证据保留」评测框架及「证据召回与最终准确率排名不一致」的发现，可供核查 LVR 中视觉／上下文证据筛选与压缩的评测设计；但论文仅限文本且不涉及 latent 内部状态，迁移到多模态证据筛选需进一步判断。
